questions.q: What state does a newly created Bulk API 2.0 ingest job start in?
questions.explain: A newly created ingest job starts in the Open state, ready to receive CSV data uploads.

questions.q: What PATCH call is required to actually start processing an ingest job's uploaded data?
options: No PATCH call is required; processing starts automatically after the first upload
questions.explain: Setting the job's state to UploadComplete is the required signal that upload is finished — processing never begins without this call.

questions.q: What HTTP method and content type are used to upload CSV data to an ingest job's batches endpoint?
questions.explain: Uploading CSV data to .../jobs/ingest/{id}/batches is a PUT request with a text/csv Content-Type.

questions.q: Why should you check failedResults even when a job's overall state is JobComplete?
options: JobComplete only describes that the job finished processing — individual records within it can still have failed validation independently
failedResults is only populated when the job's state is Failed, never JobComplete
Checking failedResults is optional and never necessary once a job reaches JobComplete
JobComplete means every record succeeded by definition, so failedResults is always empty
questions.explain: A job can complete overall while some of its individual records failed, which is exactly why successfulResults and failedResults are reported separately.

questions.q: Which three result endpoints does a completed Bulk API 2.0 ingest job expose?
questions.explain: A completed job separates its outcomes into successfulResults, failedResults, and unprocessedrecords, each retrieved as its own CSV response.
